page.layout: One column of running text; narrow notes in the right margin, cut off at the scan edge; a neighbouring page edge at the far right. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.p: nec fedimentum in urinâ ; plerum-que arguit naturam non esse aggref-fam concoctionem ; at si interdum appareant, rursumque evanescant naturæ & morbi certamen innuunt. Quod si in morbis nulla appareant contenta,ut quandoque accidit; cru-ditatis magnæ , aut corruptionis hu-morum est argumentum.quod & ac-cidit in viscerum debilitate. inflam-matione , aut obstructione. Si præ-cesserint magnæ evacuationes , hu-mores excrementitios expurgantes destituitur urina contentis. Quod in sanis contentorum defectus ab ob-structione fiat;non est admittendum illi enim sæpè non gignunt. Multa contenta in ægris fiunt à validâ fa-cultate alteratrice ; quæ in febrium initiis & augmento copiam humo-rũ designant ; in declinatione auten-si appareant ; modo nullum pravum interveniat signum; salutem & secu-ritatem denunciant. Pus sæpe in urì-nâ subsidens, mentitur bonam hypo-stasin;distinguitur tamen,quia puru[illegible, ~8 letters]

page.notes: The right margin carries several short notes, cut off by the scan edge and mostly illegible (fragments such as "Eventur", "partem", "Horum", "lenta urina", "cacea, pultacea"); they are not transcribed. The final word of the page, "puru", continues into the catchword "lent" printed at the lower right. Words at line ends with a printed hyphen are kept as printed. Some letters in the main text (e.g. "urì-nâ", "rũ") are uncertain from the scan but were read as printed.
